The Montparnasse derailment occurred on October 22, 1895 when the Granville–Paris Express overran the buffer stop at its Gare Montparnasse terminus. With the train several minutes late and the driver trying to make up for lost time, it entered the station too fast and the train air brake failed. After running through the buffer stop, the train crossed the 100 foot wide station concourse and crashed through the 2 foot thick station wall, then fell 33 feet onto the Place de Rennes below, where it stood on its nose. A woman in the street below was killed by falling masonry.
